class.name: PolyMeshBuilder4D
class.brief_description: Functions for creating and modifying 4D polyhedral meshes.
class.description: PolyMeshBuilder4D is a singleton for creating and modifying 4D polyhedral meshes. It contains all functions important enough to be included in the 4D module, but too complex to be included in [ArrayPolyMesh4D], and not important enough to have their own dedicated types. For example, creating a subdivided 4D box is handled by [BoxPolyMesh4D], not by this class.

method.name: convert_mesh_3d_to_4d_faces_only
method.description: Converts a 3D [Mesh] into a 4D [ArrayPolyMesh4D] by copying the vertex positions, inferring the edges of faces, and translating the faces to use those edges. If [param which_surface] is -1, then all surfaces are used, otherwise the specified surface is used. If [param deduplicate] is true, then vertices and edges will be deduplicated so that vertices with the same position will be merged into a single vertex, otherwise separate vertices and edges in the input will be kept separate. The resulting mesh will have no 3D cells or 4D volumes, only the 2D faces brought in with as minimal modifications as possible. After conversion, the mesh can be further modified with other functions in this class to extrude the 2D faces into 3D cells and/or 4D volumes to build a 4D mesh.

method.name: delete_interior
method.description: Deletes the interior of a poly mesh, meaning any interior 3D cells shared by two 4D volumes, as well as all 4D volumes and all higher-dimensional elements. This operates on [param mesh_4d], in place, turning a solid poly mesh into its boundary. Any 3D cells shared by two volumes are considered to be structural scaffolding on the interior of the mesh. These cells do not result in any visible geometry and are not rendered. Returns the number of 3D cells deleted. A mesh without volumes is left unchanged. Any bindings associated with the deleted elements are also removed. This is the counterpart of [method extrude_linear] on a mesh with cells, whose output has one volume per input cell and an interior cell between each pair of adjacent input cells.

method.name: extrude_linear
method.description: Extrudes a 3D mesh into 4D by creating 2 copies of the input mesh's data, translating one copy by the [param extrusion_vector] and the other copy by the negative of the [param extrusion_vector], and then connecting the corresponding 2D faces into new 3D cells. This operation is similar to Blender's "Mesh → Extrude → Extrude Faces" operation (hotkey "E"), but Blender's operation extrudes the 2D faces of a 3D mesh, while this function extrudes the 3D cells of a 4D mesh. Also, unlike Blender's operation, this function extrudes in both directions at once, and extrudes the entire mesh at once instead of allowing selection of which cells to extrude. The input mesh MUST have both 2D faces and 3D cells defined in the [member ArrayPolyMesh4D.poly_cell_indices] array. This means that [member ArrayPolyMesh4D.poly_cell_indices] MUST have a length of at least 2. The two copies of the input mesh's 3D cells become the caps of the extruded shape, and are oriented to face away from each other along the [param extrusion_vector]. The input's normal and texture map bindings are carried onto the two copies, and its per-face normals also orient the new cells, but nothing is derived for the new faces and edges, so the bindings below the cell level come out covering only the copies. [method ArrayPolyMesh4D.delete_normals_below_dimension] and [method ArrayPolyMesh4D.delete_texture_maps_below_dimension] remove them once they are no longer wanted, which for a texture map made for the input is usually right away.

method.name: extrude_spin_from_faces_xw
method.description: Extrudes a 3D mesh into 4D by creating many copies of the input mesh's data, rotating each copy incrementally in the XW plane, and then connecting the corresponding 2D faces into new 3D cells. This operation is similar to Blender's "Mesh → Extrude → Spin" operation, but Blender's operation uses the 1D edges of a 2D mesh to create the 2D faces of a 3D mesh, while this function uses the 2D faces of a 3D mesh to create the 3D cells of a 4D mesh. Also, unlike Blender's operation, this function extrudes the entire mesh at once instead of allowing selection of which faces to extrude. This operation is also known as lathe, revolve, or sweep in some 3D modeling software. The input mesh MUST have 2D faces defined in the [member ArrayPolyMesh4D.poly_cell_indices] array, and MUST NOT have any 3D cells or 4D volumes defined. This means that [member ArrayPolyMesh4D.poly_cell_indices] MUST have a length of exactly 1. The input mesh SHOULD NOT have significant vertex positions on the W axis. The input mesh SHOULD only exist in one radial direction, for example, only existing in +X and not -X. The input mesh SHOULD have 1D edges converging to zero along both the X and W axes, or else the resulting mesh will have holes.

method.name: make_boundary_normals_topologically_consistent
method.description: Makes the boundary normals of a 4D polyhedral mesh topologically consistent by ensuring that all boundary cells that share a common face have the same normal direction. The [param authoritative_boundary_cells] parameter specifies a list of boundary cell indices that are considered authoritative for determining the normal direction. Their normals will be preserved, and any adjacent non-authoritative boundary cells will be flipped if necessary to match the authoritative normals, recursively propagating in a flood-fill manner. [b]Note:[/b] This function only works correctly if the input mesh has star-shaped polyhedral boundary cells, and if it can locate a point within the star-shaped region of that cell. For non-convex cells, you may need to set [member ArrayPolyMesh4D.poly_cell_boundary_pivot_overrides] to specify where the pivot point is located in the cells.

method.name: make_cells_from_manifold_sheets
method.description: Groups the faces of a faces-only mesh into manifold sheets and appends one 3D cell per sheet, in place, returning how many cells were made. A manifold sheet is a set of faces connected through edges that exactly two faces use, the way the faces of a surface connect. A border edge, used by one face, connects nothing. An edge used by three or more faces, such as where a partition wall meets an outer wall, is a junction between sheets rather than part of one, so the outer wall stays one sheet running through the junction while the partition is its own sheet. A sheet also stays within one 3D hyperplane: a face whose vertices leave the sheet's hyperplane by more than [param angle_tolerance_radians], measured as an angle relative to the size of that face, is not connected through that edge, so a surface bending into the fourth dimension is split where it bends. While the faces of a sheet are still coplanar, several neighbors may leave their plane in different directions, and the sheet takes the hyperplane that the most of those neighbors agree with, so that a single stray face cannot claim it. [b]Note:[/b] These cells are sheets, not the volumes a 3D mesh encloses. Two boxes sharing a face yield two open cells of five faces each, with the shared face in neither, because every edge of the shared face is a three-face junction. This grouping is what mitered offsets need, since a corner may only be shared between faces that meet along an edge of their own. Grouping faces into the enclosed volumes instead, where the shared face would belong to both cells, would be a different operation. Nor are sheets merely disconnected pieces: faces that only touch at a vertex, or only along a junction edge, are separate sheets even though the mesh is connected. This turns a 3D mesh brought in through [method convert_mesh_3d_to_4d_faces_only] into cells, which [method ArrayPolyMesh4D.calculate_boundary_normals] and the decomposition into tetrahedra for rendering need, since a mesh without cells has no volume to show. The mesh must not already have cells; delete them first if it does. The faces themselves are left as they are, including their orientation and any bindings, and no edges are added. Each cell lists its faces in the order they were found, starting with the lowest-index face of the sheet, and prefers a second face out of the plane of the first, since two coplanar first faces, such as the two triangles of a quad, would give the cell a degenerate orientation. Consider running [method merge_coplanar_faces] first. A sheet of fewer than 4 faces, or whose faces are all coplanar, cannot be a valid 3D cell enclosing a volume, so it is left out with a warning and its faces stay as faces only.

method.name: make_coplanar
method.description: Splits every element whose vertices do not lie in a flat space of its own dimension, such as a 2D plane for a 2D face, or a 3D hyperplane for a 3D cell. The resulting elements will be flat in the space. This is an in-place operation which modifies the given mesh. Returns how many splits were made. An element is flat when its vertices stay within [param angle_tolerance_radians] of such a flat, relative to its size. A split cuts off one vertex: the element's boundary is divided into the parts that have the vertex and the parts that do not, and a new element of the dimension below closes both sides, a diagonal edge for a face or a face through the surrounding edges for a cell, so a face loses a triangle and a cell loses a pyramid. The vertex cut off is the one whose removal leaves the rest closest to flat, then the one standing farthest out of the flat through the rest, then the one with the smallest cut, so a box face with one corner raised is cut along its level diagonal into a flat triangle and a leaning one, and a polygon with one raised corner loses only that corner's triangle. Faces are split before cells, and a cut that is not flat itself is split in turn, so every dimension is flat once this returns. The pieces, the elements above them, and the bindings follow [method ArrayPolyMesh4D.split_poly_element], which does the bookkeeping. The cross-sections that a 4D mesh renders are only flat when its 3D cells are, and [method solidify_faces] and [method extrude_linear] give flat cells only from flat faces, which is what this is for.

method.name: merge_coplanar_faces
method.description: Merges adjacent faces that lie in the same plane into single faces, in place, and returns how many merges were made. Two faces are merged when they share an edge, every vertex of one lies in the plane of the other within [param angle_tolerance_radians] (measured as the angle of each vertex's offset out of the plane), and the merged polygon is convex, since faces are triangulated as fans. The edges that were interior to the merged faces are deleted. This repairs faces that were needlessly split, such as quads triangulated by a glTF export and brought in through [method convert_mesh_3d_to_4d_faces_only], or faces of a convex hull whose coplanarity was lost to quantization. Cells keep referencing the merged faces and keep their orientation and boundary normals. Every normal and texture map binding is carried over: each merged face takes its values from the faces it absorbed, and the bindings of edges, cells, and 4D cells follow their surviving sub-elements. An element whose values cannot all be found in its sources, such as a face merged from a mapped and an unmapped triangle, ends up with an empty entry, meaning missing data. Faces must have their edges stored in loop order, which every built-in mesh source provides.

method.name: reconstruct_from_tetra_mesh
method.description: Reconstructs a polyhedral mesh from a tetrahedral mesh by converting each consecutive sequence of tetrahedral cells with the same starting vertex into a single polyhedral cell, forming a new cell when the starting vertex changes. This function is useful for converting tetrahedral meshes into polyhedral meshes when the polyhedral structure is implied by the ordering of the tetrahedral cells and a polyhedral representation is desired for further processing. However, this operation is lossy, and so round-trip conversions may not yield the original data. Whenever possible, always keep the original polyhedral mesh data and work with that directly, and avoid using this function unless absolutely necessary.

method.name: solidify_faces
method.description: Thickens the 2D faces of a mesh into solid 3D cells within the 3D hyperplane perpendicular to [param hyperplane_normal], the way Blender's Solidify modifier thickens a 3D surface, and returns the result as a new mesh. Each face becomes a cell made of two offset copies of the face and a wall over each of its edges, [param thickness] apart along the face's normal within the hyperplane. The mesh does not have to lie in the hyperplane: the offsets are taken within it and whatever the positions have along [param hyperplane_normal] is kept, so the outline of a fence on uneven ground gives a slab that follows the ground and is as thick as requested everywhere. A face that leans out of the hyperplane is thickened on its own, never mitered with its neighbors, and has to be flat: every cell must fit a 3D hyperplane for its cross-sections to be flat, which the cell of a leaning face only does when its corners move along the face's own normal, while a level face, with all of its vertices at one position along [param hyperplane_normal], may be warped and mitered freely. A face perpendicular to the hyperplane has no normal within it and cannot be solidified. With an [param offset] of [code]0.0[/code] the copies sit half the thickness to either side of the face, with [code]1.0[/code] the whole thickness lies on the side the face's normal points to, and with [code]-1.0[/code] on the other side. The per-face normals are used when the mesh has one for every face, and are otherwise computed as by [method PolyMesh4D.compute_face_normals]. Where faces meet at a vertex, their copies share mitered corners, offset so that every face's plane moves by exactly the same distance, the way a mitered joint keeps a beam as thick around a corner as along it. A corner is only shared between faces of the same group: the mesh's 3D cells when it has them, with each face in at most one cell, and manifold sheets as [method make_cells_from_manifold_sheets] finds them among the level faces in no cell, so a partition wall meeting an outer wall is thickened on its own and ends inside the wall rather than distorting it. The faces of a group are oriented consistently before mitering, so the orientation of a face relative to its neighbors does not matter, and the direction of [param offset] follows the group's first face. A sharp corner's offset is clamped to [param miter_limit] times the distance the faces move, which is never less than that distance itself. The faces must have their edges stored in loop order. The output has a per-face normal for every face, with each copy facing out of the solid and each wall facing away from its face, its cells oriented along [param hyperplane_normal], and the input's face-corner normals and texture maps carried onto both copies of each face; other bindings are not carried over. A wall between two faces of the same group is interior to the solid and shared by both of their cells, so extruding the result with [method extrude_linear] and then calling [method delete_interior] leaves only its boundary, which is how a beam is made from a fence's 2D outline.

method.name: subdivide_elements
method.description: Subdivides the selected elements of the given dimension, in place, returning the indices of the new elements created from the selected ones, so that callers can keep track of the inputs, such as updating a user's selection in a modeling tool. If [param elements] is empty, all elements of the given dimension are subdivided. Repeat the subdivision for finer detail. The subdivision splits all edges at their midpoints, and uses well-proportioned decompositions per shape: triangles subdivide into 4 similar triangles, other polygons subdivide into quadrilaterals around a center vertex, simplexes subdivide into corner simplexes and a central rectified simplex (a tetrahedron becomes 4 tetrahedra and an octahedron), boxes subdivide into 8 sub-boxes, orthoplexes subdivide into corner orthoplexes and simplex cones (an octahedron becomes 6 octahedra and 8 tetrahedra), and any other cell is subdivided by connecting its centroid to every piece of its subdivided boundary. Elements below the selected ones are always fully subdivided too. Unselected elements above or beside them are conformed by referencing the pieces of their subdivided members, which keeps the mesh crack-free, even under deformation, because the pieces are shared rather than duplicated. Boundary normals, boundary cell vertex normals, and cell texture maps are carried over and interpolated (or the per-face equivalents, for a flat mesh with only 2D faces), boundary cells keep their normals and matching orientations, sub-elements of seam faces stay seams, and subdividing 4D volumetric cells creates interior boundary cells that are excluded from rendering. [b]Note:[/b] For the best results, subdivide all desired elements in a single call. A conformed cell is no longer shaped like a simplex, box, or orthoplex, so subdividing it in a later call falls back to the centroid-based subdivision.
